_comment: Wave 5 -- the shop-aware mechanism, retested with a demand model that matches this engine. _remaining_drain is the only code in the agent that reads town.unlocked_shops, and it overestimates by 1.3-1.8x on most products and 4.7-6.7x on melon, measured against 200 real ladder shop draws. It feeds _race_factor, which adds slot priority for a product whose remaining supply outruns the town's remaining appetite. _RACE_WEIGHT tested harmful in wave 1 (mirror) and neutral in wave 4 (field) -- both with the broken model.
_why_this_and_not_production: Production cannot respond to the shop draw without writing a new agent. PLANT names its crop in the action (`["PLANT", "CARROT"]`), and the engine drops ALL plant requests for a crop when seeds are short, so editing the market queue's BUY_SEED orders redirects nothing and can destroy a whole turn's planting. Selling is the only part of the loop the tape leaves open.
_the_prize_being_chased: Shop draw is worth 64% to 98% win rate against four mined ladder lines, and the milk market closes at $1 with three or fewer milk shops, $47 with four, $197 with five. Any dial that lets the agent notice which markets will stay liquid is aimed at that spread.

_notes.r0_is_a_replicate: _race_factor returns 1.0 when _RACE_WEIGHT <= 0, so the drain model is unreachable at r0. The donor and fixed cells at r0 must return identical numbers; if they do not, _X_DRAIN_FIX is leaking somewhere it should not.
_notes.expected_direction: Written before the run. The corrected model reports LESS remaining demand, so more products look structurally oversupplied, so _race_factor fires more often and harder. If wave 1's finding was 'racing is bad', a truer model should make it worse, not better. A win here would mean the earlier harm came from racing the wrong products.
